### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **70** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc173343ea57fb854994a9d59e9145a52656f8e9`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/meta (route, 55 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **189** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc173343ea57fb854994a9d59e9145a52656f8e9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `27f927fbc6dfc597e3275bf344789fee9cb5d7be` — the merge of head `8bfa49aef9aca369ac6a3d22c3628d66885d3a0e` into base `bc173343ea57fb854994a9d59e9145a52656f8e9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 27f927fbc6dfc597e3275bf344789fee9cb5d7be && git checkout 27f927fbc6dfc597e3275bf344789fee9cb5d7be
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bc173343ea57fb854994a9d59e9145a52656f8e9 8bfa49aef9aca369ac6a3d22c3628d66885d3a0e && git checkout -B drift-repro bc173343ea57fb854994a9d59e9145a52656f8e9 && git merge --no-ff 8bfa49aef9aca369ac6a3d22c3628d66885d3a0e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc173343ea57fb854994a9d59e9145a52656f8e9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bc173343ea57fb854994a9d59e9145a52656f8e9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #37856: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37924: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `a2dd88a68cbb2efa6145ad4b2cdf9100ba802e28`
  · the check-runs on `a2dd88a68cbb2efa6145ad4b2cdf9100ba802e28`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the narrowing is declared of the whole PR, never of a path: the floor is EVERY path of the diff outside the
  prose faces (the 83 paths listed in SCRATCHPAD/pr-37924/scope-paths.txt), plus every file those hunks make a claim about, read in the cited code.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below that floor; the record's `Scope:` line lists both. No path is the lane seat's remainder.
  ④ judges the narrowing itself over that floor: lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in
  the PR are not reviewed; the published spec and the cited code are READ to judge it, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `SCRATCHPAD/pr-37924/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — the narrowing itself, read against the published spec on `main`: does it take a
     declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real? A capability declared
     and not delivered is an implementation gap, implemented or retired, ⛔ never narrowed at the consumer.
     Read the spec and the cited code in the live tree, and try to break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, `ActionType`**: `ask_ai` leaves the members; `enumWithRetiredValues` answers it with the prescription. Right: ADR-0160 D7 "One prescription, on the enum". `ActionType.options` is now the six live members, so `TARGET_REQUIRED_TYPES` and `ROW_BUILTIN_EXECUTORS` lose `ask_ai` with it. Right.
- **Accept-set, an action's own `type`** (`actionObject`, which `ActionSchema` and `InlineActionSchema` both build on): the second enum answers `ask_ai` with the same sentence. Right (ADR point 29).
- **Accept-set, page action rows**: `refuseRowRetiredAskAi` on `actionType` of `action:button` / `action:icon` and on `type` of `action:group` / `action:menu` members. On main these open strings accepted `ask_ai`; now refused. Right (ADR point 29). This is the real narrowing beside the enum.
- **Dashboard header `actionType`**: main already refused `ask_ai` there (`refuseRecordlessAskAi`); the PR swaps that refusal for the enum's prescription. No accept-set change, the message changes. Right. `WidgetActionTypeSchema` has no other user, so no dashboard conversion is owed.
- **Removed refinements**: `refuseAskAiContradictions` on `ActionSchema` and `InlineActionSchema`, `TARGETLESS_TYPES`. They judged only an `ask_ai` action, which no longer parses. Right.
- **Public surface, spec**: `applyConversionsToStoredItem` returns `T | undefined` (a widened return type on a root export); `ConversionContext` gains optional `atRest`; `removePageComponents` is new in `walk.ts`; `ACTION_TYPE_VALUES` and `ASK_AI_RETIRED` are not exported. Right, and the changeset names the first two.
- **Conversion `action-type-ask-ai-removed`** (major 19, `retiredFromLoadPath`, `retiredAfter: '18.6.0'`): matches D7 "The ADR-0087 kit". The two doors are told apart as D7 leaves to this card: `applyMetaMigrations` calls `conversion.apply` with no context, so `atRest` is unset over sources and the name guard runs; `applyConversions` sets `atRest` exactly when `includeRetired` is set, which only the stored seam, the artifact door and the fixture CI pass (flow replay passes it too and this entry walks no flow). Right. The guard collects every string value outside the `ask_ai` entries, a superset of the exact-name references `ACTION_NAME_UNDEFINED` walks. Right, and conservative.
- **Artifact door**: out of the diff. Read: a floor of 19.0.0 at a 19.0.0 runtime opens the entry through the major-step half; a floor below the runtime replays the whole chain; a floor past 19.0.0 keeps the strict parse. That is the window D7.3 describes ("every build made during the 19 prerelease"). Right.
- **D3 entry `ui-action-type-ask-ai-retired`**: registered, names the hand edits, carries `conversionIds`. Right.
- **Stored seam, callers that needed no change**: `convertStoredItem` / `convertStoredItemDetailed`, `withDeclaredPageTypeDefault`, `withRowBinding`, `decorateMetadataItem`, the stored-collection fold, ObjectQL's `readAuthoredActionRows` / hook rows, and the active arm of `getMetaItem` all pass `undefined` through or skip it. No path registers or dereferences an undefined item. No other registered conversion empties a top-level collection, so no other row type newly answers `undefined`. Right. Two out-of-diff readers answer wrongly: see S1.
- **`DatabaseLoader`**: `rowToData` answers `null` for the row and the type-wide read skips it; identity (slot, member, unnamed-row naming) reads the stored body through `rowIdentityData`. `exists`, `list` and `delete` work off the name column and the stored body. Holds against the code.
- **`migrateStoredMetadata`**: the `item === undefined` branch sits after the `changed` test and before both the preview and the apply arm, records `skipped` with the delete instruction and writes nothing. Holds.
- **Runtime and ui removals**: every removed symbol exists only for `ask_ai` on main (`bulkRefusal` included: its one body is `isAskAiAction`). `resolveAiApiBase` moves back into `useAiSurface.ts`, still exported. The three Studio canvas strings stay. Right.
- **Blast radius on main**: showcase action, its page reference and its translation key are removed by hand (D7.2 names this case). `skills/objectstack-ai` teaching and eval: PR #37937, which is open and not merged as read. `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md:151` and `:153`: knowingly left, carrier #37857. The two `.changeset/pre/` notes: left, corrected in this changeset, carrier the release owner. brightrule: carrier its owner. hotcrm and cloud: none per the card; not re-read here.
- **`Fixes #37827`**: correct. That card asked for the record page to draw `ask_ai` actions; the maintainer's ruling retires the type, the card's own two re-block comments name #37856 as its closer, card #37856 step 7 orders it, and the branch holds a claim on it. With the handler gone there is nothing left to fix.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` stand on both the PR body and the changeset. The kind is right: an accepted value is now refused.
- Level: `@objectstack/spec` `minor` meets "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves". The other packages at `patch` or `minor` are within the rule; nothing is `major`.
- Banner, FROM and TO rows, the one-line fix and the ADR-0087 marker (`registered action-type-ask-ai-removed, ui-action-type-ask-ai-retired`) are present and match the diff. Both registered ids exist in the tree.

The card's acceptance line "brightrule boots on the new version" is not shown by this PR; the card puts it before C1 releases, not before merge. Escalated to the seat as an open carrier.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away at a consumer. ADR-0160 D7 on main (seventh amendment) retires the type by the maintainer's ruling, and the type was published only on `19.0.0-next.0`. The refusal, the conversion's two doors, the D3 entry, the `undefined` answer of the stored seam and the `skipped` listing each match the text of D7 and points 29 to 31. Tried and held: an unnamed action deleted over sources while a reference survives (the string superset prevents it within one stack); a second conversion emptying a collection; an undefined item reaching a registry write; the identity read losing a row's object binding; the artifact window missing a prerelease build.

S1 (should-fix) — two stored-row readers outside the diff treat the seam's `undefined` as a served body, so a row that should be served is masked. D7.3 says no read returns the action and what carried it still loads.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`, the `previewDrafts` arm (about line 1085): for a draft row that is an `ask_ai` action, `draftItem` is `undefined`, the address test passes (`exactQualifierItem` hands `undefined` back) and the read returns `item: undefined` at once. It never reaches the active row or the registry, so a published action with a pending `ask_ai` draft reads as nothing on a preview read. The list read's draft arm was fixed in this PR (`.filter`), the by-name arm was not.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` (lines 592, 731, then 637, 661 and 884): `overlay` is initialised to `null` and every later test is `overlay !== null`. An `undefined` overlay therefore counts as present: `overlayScope` is `'env'`, the row-less view expansion is skipped, and `effective` is `undefined` instead of `code`. A packaged action under a stored `ask_ai` row of the same name loses its effective layer on the editor read, while `getMetaItem` serves it. Line 943 already tests `overlay !== undefined`, which shows the two states were not meant to differ.
- Fix: map `undefined` to "no row" at both sites (fall through in the preview arm; `?? null` on the three layered assignments), with a test for each.

S2 (should-fix) — D7.3 charges this card to pin by test that the delete door still reaches such a row, and names that door as the metadata API's delete. The `skipped` reason sends the operator to `DELETE /api/v1/meta/action/NAME`. The pin in the diff is on `DatabaseLoader.delete`; the metadata API's delete is `deleteMetaItem`, which goes through `SysMetadataRepository`, and the protocol test's stub engine deletes nothing.
